name: Casey's General Stores, Inc.
moat_justification: Rural/small-town store density that national rivals can't economically replicate, plus a prepared-food program (pizza, 59.3% Q1 FY27 segment margin) that turns a commodity fuel stop into a food destination; scale in distribution, private brand, and a 10M+ member rewards program; OE positive 5/5 years. Against: zero switching costs, fuel is ~60% of revenue at commodity street-priced margins and the recent earnings driver (fuel margin per gallon) is cyclical and outside management's control, long-run EV erosion of the fuel hook, labor/credit-card fee pressure, and acquisition integration risk from Fikes/CEFCO.
fragility_flags: NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025, 2026 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 3.6x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: High-quality rural convenience compounder, moat 6/10 — but priced for perfection: weighted IRR 5.66% and IV@15% $155.81 vs the $664.19 price; it only clears the 15% hurdle at or below ~$156.
moat_for: Rural/small-town density rivals can't replicate store-by-store
Prepared-food brand with ~59% segment margins (pizza destination)
Scale: own distribution, private brand, 10M+ rewards members
OE positive 5/5 years; compounding through cycles
Owns much of its real estate
moat_against: No switching costs — loyalty is habit/location only
Fuel ~60% of revenue at commodity, street-priced margins
Fuel margin (recent earnings driver) is cyclical, not controlled
Long-run EV adoption erodes the fuel-traffic hook
Labor and credit-card fee inflation on store opex
Acquisition-led growth: Fikes/CEFCO integration and debt load
